summary: Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD from UCLA (2010) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and has held posts at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (all attested 2010).

Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Australian National University and earned his PhD at Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman (~1989–1994), later holding posts at SOAS (~1996–1998) and the University of Sydney (~2002).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held a post as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2004) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley in ~2005.

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford and the University of Exeter (PhD 1987–1990). He lectured at the Workers' Educational Association and the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) before serving at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as a history professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).

Mark I. Wallace works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (~1982–1986) and held posts at Merrimack College, Georgia State University, and Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1929–1937) and Utrecht University (~1937–1941) under Jan Gonda, later teaching Iranian languages at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).

Mark Juergensmeyer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Illinois and UC Berkeley (PhD ~1965–1974), holding major posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College (~2020).

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. His academic posts include serving as assistant professor at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and Associate Professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006).
Mark Owen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski studied Indology, philosophy, and religious studies at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Oxford (PhD ~1975–1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), alongside traditional teachers.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served at Illinois State University (~1979–2008) and later held the post of Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Seoul National University (~2008–2012).

Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge. He has held a post as Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

Mark T. Unno is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University (~1987–1994) and held posts at Brown University (~1994–1996) and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (1978) and served as a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).

Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD (~1989–1996) at Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University (1994–1999), and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn. He has held posts at the University of Bonn (~2009), UC Berkeley, The New School (~2012–2013), and the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy (2024).

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (-2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and held positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) and Heidelberg University.

Marsha Weidner works in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Sahlins was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), later holding faculty posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (1973).
